## ✨ Highlights

- 📊 **More on a node's page**: which IP version clients come over, each backend's throughput now in a sortable table, the LOGS partition beside STATE, backends as a list, stick tables drawn as tables on the Traffic flow, and each connection's throughput on Monitoring › Network.
- 📈 **The exporters listen on the node's main interface by default** - the one its default route leaves by - instead of every address. Nodes set up before keep every address.

## 📊 The node's page

- **Metrics** ([#239](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/239)):
  - **IP versions**: how many of the requests in HAProxy's last log lines came over IPv4 and over IPv6, counted from the access log lines the TLS cards already read. Shown once the node has an IPv6 address of its own, or a client came over IPv6.
  - **Errors and refusals** (bad and denied requests, denied connections and responses, failed connections and responses, retries, redispatches) and **Traffic by frontend**, from the counters the page already reads.
  - However many cards there are, their last row is full - no lone card leaves a gap.
  - **Backends: how fast they answer** sorts by any column and shows each backend's bytes a second **in and out** now.
- **Overview**: the **LOGS** partition as a gauge beside STATE, with the boots it holds. It's a ring that fills by design: it never turns amber or red.
- **Apps › HAProxy › Backends**: **Cards or List** - the list has a row per server of every backend (address, state, Ready/Drain/Maint), filtered and sorted. The choice is remembered per browser, like the node list's.
- **Traffic flow**: a backend that only holds a **stick table** (`backend st_abuse` + `stick-table`, which frontend rules track clients into) is drawn as a table, no longer red ("DOWN") and dashed ("no rule names it"); its details show the entries used. A backend with servers names its table in its details.
- **Monitoring › Network** ([#239](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/239), [#240](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/240)): the sockets filtered by **IP version**, and each TCP connection's **receiving and sending** bytes a second, sortable - the node now gives each connection's byte counters (`janusctl system netstat` shows them too).

## 📈 Exporters

- **The Janus exporter and node_exporter listen on the main interface by default** ([#241](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/241), [where it listens](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/metrics.md#where-it-listens)):
  - The main interface is the one the node's IPv4 default route leaves by; on it, one address per IP version. Keepalived's virtual addresses and BGP's anycast addresses never count.
  - They follow the network: a configuration applied on trial, confirmed or reverted moves them with it.
  - `janusctl system metrics|node-exporter -address auto` (the default), `'*'` (every address) or an IP; the Controller's exporter pages have the same choice ("Listen on") and show where to scrape.
  - **Nodes set up before keep listening on every address**: their first boot on this version saves that as their setting. `-address auto` moves them.

## 🖥️ Controller

- **Single sign-on** ([#237](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/237)):
  - An identity whose name a local account already has: the message now says how to link it - sign in with the account's password, then link from the dialog under your name -, and the refusal's page offers to do just that, the dialog opening by itself on the right provider.
  - A browser trusted for the second factor asks for it before linking, as for an SSH key.
  - The account dialog says how the session signed in: through which provider, or with a password.
  - The provider form says what its **ID** is: a short name of your choosing, on the Controller only, never sent to the provider - not its client ID.

## 🔧 Node

- **A reboot logs where its time went** ([#234](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/234)): Reboot, Shutdown, Reset, Upgrade and Rollback log one line with each step's time (HAProxy stopped, shutdown hooks, sync) just before the machine goes down - to tell janusd's time from the kernel's, the firmware's or the hypervisor's (a rare slow update reboot seen in the lab).

## 🧪 Tests and tooling

- Real enforcing boots check where the exporters listen (`qemu-metrics-test`, `qemu-network-config-test` - a trial moving the default route moves them -, `qemu-extensions-test`), that a node of the previous release keeps every address after its update and after a rollback (`qemu-lifecycle-upgrade-from-release-test`), and that Netstat counts the bytes of janusctl's and the Controller's own connections.
- The runners' Docker build cache is capped and the Controller's release tags tidied ([#235](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/235)): v2026.10.22-2's publishing ran out of disk.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Nodes**: update them for the exporters' new default and the per-connection counters. A node set up before keeps its exporters on every address - nothing to do unless you want the main interface (`-address auto`). When a node's default route goes out by the network HAProxy serves (a front network with the gateway, a management network without), give the exporters the management address instead.
- **Prometheus**: a target scraped through another address than the main interface's stops answering on a node that moves to `auto` (or a new node) - scrape the main interface's address, or set the exporter's address.
- **Going back to an older version** after setting an exporter to `auto` explicitly: the older janusd doesn't know `auto`, refuses that setting and runs its defaults (every address) until the node is updated again.
- **The Controller**: update it from its page, as usual. The new pages need nodes on this version for the per-connection throughput (older nodes show "–"); everything else works with older nodes.
